newsitem.title: USA: U.S. pulls out embassy dependents from Tajikistan.
newsitem.headline: U.S. pulls out embassy dependents from Tajikistan.

text.p: The United States said on Friday it was temporarily evacuating dependents of its embassy staff in Tajikistan because of worsening security in the turbulent Central Asian country.

State Department spokesman Glyn Davies said the move was prompted by the killing on Tuesday by unidentified gunmen of two embassy security guards, locally hired ethnic Russians who Washington says were off-duty at the time.
"That was the trigger for taking this action," Davies told reporters.
The guards were among seven people -- including five Russians -- gunned down in separate attacks on Tuesday in the Tajik capital Dushanbe.

No one has claimed responsibility for the killings, widely blamed on fighters of the country's Islamist opposition who have battled the former Soviet republic's secular government over the past four years.

Davies said a total of five dependents were being pulled out on scheduled flights, leaving 12 embassy staff in place. About 65 private Americans in Tajikistan were being informed of the move but were not being advised to leave, he said.
"It's true that thus far only ethnic Russians have been targeted but in our judgment the situation is such that we should also bring dependents out, and we're doing that," Davies said.
An official statement issued later said the withdrawal was temporary and would be reviewed in 30 days to see if the situation had improved.
Reports from Dushanbe said the murdered security guards were dressed in distinctive uniforms with special badges and sleeve chevrons with U.S. flags.

The killings occurred a day after the end of a 14-day hostage crisis that highlighted the instability of Tajikistan, an impoverished country bordering China and Afghanistan. Russian and Western hostages were held by a rebel group in a standoff with the government.
The U.S. statement said Washington was concerned "about the inability of the local government to ensure the safety of international personnel, including American citizens".
Refrring to the hostage incident, it said: "We cannot rule out another move by the same people to take hostages again."
Tajikistan's President Imomali Rakhmonov and opposition leader Sayid Abdullo Nuri signed accords on Friday after peace talks in Iran, state-run Tehran radio said.
The accords, signed in the northeast Iranian city of Mashhad, included an agreement on each side's quota in a future Commission of National Reconciliation, it said.
